skill.name: aws-cost-cleanup
skill.description: Identify unused AWS resources, estimate savings, and plan guarded cleanup workflows with AWS CLI, Python, Lambda, and lifecycle policies.
skill.summary: Find AWS waste and prepare reviewed cleanup automation.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The 36 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inert shebangs, constrained read-only command substitutions, commented commands, and official AWS documentation links. Separate semantic review found destructive EBS and S3 automation that can modify live resources without enforced approval, backup, ownership, or dry-run controls.

remediation.issue: The Lambda deletes available EBS volumes using only age and attachment status.
remediation.suggestion: Default to reporting, require an explicit cleanup tag and approved volume list, verify snapshots and dependencies, and require confirmation before deletion.

remediation.issue: The S3 example applies a lifecycle policy containing expiration behavior directly to a bucket.
remediation.suggestion: Read and preserve existing rules, show a policy diff, validate retention requirements, and require an explicit bucket and confirmation before applying changes.

remediation.issue: The Kiro example combines discovery and removal in one autonomous request.
remediation.suggestion: Separate discovery from execution and require reviewed resource identifiers before generating or running destructive commands.

semantic_findings.title: Lambda Deletes EBS Volumes Without Enforced Safeguards
semantic_findings.description: The Lambda deletes every available volume older than seven days after only status and age checks. It omits ownership tags, snapshots, dependency checks, approval, and dry-run controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly calls delete_volume for matching account resources. The surrounding safety checklist is advisory and is not enforced by the function.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The policy explicitly expires noncurrent versions and the AWS command applies it to a live bucket. These effects are clear despite the placeholder bucket name.

content.user_title: Reduce AWS Waste with Guarded Resource Cleanup
content.value_statement: Unused AWS resources create recurring charges and operational clutter. This skill provides discovery commands, savings estimates, cleanup examples, automation patterns, and safety checks.
actual_capabilities: Lists unattached EBS volumes and estimates storage savings using AWS CLI and boto3.
Identifies old snapshots, unused Elastic IPs, and selected cleanup candidates.
Provides dry-run shell examples with destructive EBS, snapshot, and address commands commented by default.
Creates an S3 lifecycle configuration for storage transitions, version expiration, and incomplete upload cleanup.
Shows a Lambda pattern for deleting available EBS volumes older than seven days.
Demonstrates multi-account discovery and CloudWatch billing alarm configuration.
limitations: Does not verify application dependencies, ownership, retention policy, legal holds, or recovery requirements.
Uses fixed example pricing and thresholds that may not match current AWS rates or business rules.
Destructive examples require live AWS credentials and can cause irreversible data loss.
Does not implement a complete approval, audit, rollback, or multi-region orchestration system.

use_cases.title: Quantify cleanup opportunities
use_cases.description: Produce a read-only inventory and estimated monthly savings before proposing any changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare a reviewed cleanup
use_cases.description: Build a staged process for validating, approving, executing, and recording selected resource removals.

use_cases.title: Create recurring cost controls
use_cases.description: Plan lifecycle rules, cleanup schedules, and billing alarms for a small AWS environment.

prompt_templates.title: Inventory obvious waste
prompt_templates.prompt: List read-only AWS CLI commands to find unattached EBS volumes and unused Elastic IPs. Do not include deletion commands.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner discovery in one account and region.

prompt_templates.title: Estimate monthly savings
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a regional savings report for unattached EBS volumes and unused Elastic IPs. State pricing assumptions and avoid modifying resources.
prompt_templates.scenario: Read-only cost analysis with transparent assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a reviewed cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a two-phase EBS cleanup workflow. First produce a tagged inventory, then require approved volume IDs before generating deletion commands.

prompt_templates.title: Plan organization-wide automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-account cleanup system with role assumptions, tag allowlists, policy checks, approvals, audit logs, retries, and rollback procedures.

output_examples.input: Find unattached EBS volumes in us-east-1 and estimate savings.
output: Estimated monthly savings: USD 62.00 using the stated USD 0.10 per GB-month assumption.
Next step: verify ownership tags and snapshot requirements before approval.

output_examples.input: Propose an S3 lifecycle policy for older objects.
output_examples.output: Proposed change: transition objects after 90 days and expire noncurrent versions after 30 days. Review retention requirements before applying the policy.

output_examples.input: Plan cleanup discovery across member accounts.
output: Scope: enumerate active organization accounts and assume a dedicated read-only role.
Report candidates by account, region, resource type, owner tag, age, and estimated savings.
Keep execution disabled until account owners approve explicit resource identifiers.

best_practices: Begin with read-only discovery and preserve the inventory used for every approval decision.
Require resource ownership tags, dependency checks, current backups, and named approval before any destructive action.
Test in a non-production account, use least-privilege roles, and record every attempted and completed change.
anti_patterns: Do not run the destructive Lambda example unchanged in production accounts.
Do not treat unattached, stopped, or old resources as automatically safe to delete.
Do not replace existing lifecycle policies without reviewing current rules and compliance retention requirements.

faq.question: Which AWS resources does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers selected EBS, snapshot, S3, EC2, Elastic IP, networking, billing alarm, and multi-account cleanup patterns.

faq.question: Does the skill execute cleanup automatically?
faq.answer: The skill provides commands and examples. Some examples modify or delete AWS resources when a user runs or deploys them.

faq.question: Can I use it for read-only discovery?
faq.answer: Yes. Use AWS describe commands and savings calculations without enabling deletion, release, or policy-update operations.

faq.question: Are the savings estimates exact?
faq.answer: No. The examples use fixed rates and require validation against current AWS pricing, regions, volume types, and negotiated discounts.

faq.question: Does it support AWS Organizations?
faq.answer: It demonstrates account iteration, but production use needs controlled role assumptions, regional coverage, error handling, and account-level approval.

faq.question: How should I prevent accidental deletion?
faq.answer: Use read-only discovery, tag allowlists, current backups, dependency checks, explicit resource approvals, least privilege, and a separate execution step.
